name: 0002_profile_query_count_profile_query_limit.py
summary: Django schema migration that adds query_count and query_limit fields to the user Profile model.
purpose: Extends the user Profile model to support per-user query usage tracking and enforceable rate limits, enabling quota management and usage analytics directly at the database level.
responsibilities: Add query_count integer field to the Profile table to track cumulative or periodic usage
Add query_limit integer field to the Profile table to store the maximum allowed queries
Maintain a reversible, version-controlled schema change within the users app boundary
Ensure correct migration ordering by declaring dependencies on previous users app migrations
inputs: Django migration dependency graph (users app 0001_initial or prior migration)
Target database connection and current schema state
Django ORM model definition for Profile
outputs: Updated database schema with query_count and query_limit columns on the profile table
Migration history entry (django_migrations) marking version 0002 for the users app
architecture_notes: Follows Django's built-in migration framework for declarative, database-agnostic schema evolution within a modular monolith. Colocating the migration in backend/apps/users keeps user-domain schema changes aligned with the app's bounded context. Adding tracking fields directly to the Profile model favors a denormalized, read-optimized design for quick quota lookups, though it couples metering data to the core user entity. The sequential 0002 prefix implies an incremental evolution from the initial users migration.
improvements: Include a RunPython data migration to backfill sensible defaults for existing profile rows and avoid NULL states
Add database indexes on query_count if the field supports frequent filtering, sorting, or locking during enforcement
Introduce a database check constraint (query_count <= query_limit) if the RDBMS should enforce business invariants
Normalize query_limit into a separate Tier/Plan model if limits vary by subscription and require shared configuration
Consider offloading high-frequency query_count increments to a separate counter or analytics table to reduce row-lock contention on the Profile record
